questions.stem: At temperature T, compound $\mathrm{AB_{2(g)}}$ dissociates as $\mathrm{AB_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons AB_{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}B_{2(g)}}$ having degree of dissociation x (small compared to unity). The correct expression for x in terms of $K_p$ and p is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{AB_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons AB_{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}B_{2(g)}}$
$t_{eq.}$: $\dfrac{(1-x)}{1+\frac{x}{2}}P$, $\dfrac{xP}{1+\frac{x}{2}}$, $\dfrac{\frac{x}{2}P}{1+\frac{x}{2}}$
$\Rightarrow x \ll 1 \Rightarrow 1+\dfrac{x}{2} \approx 1$ and $1-x \approx 1$
$\Rightarrow k_P = \dfrac{(xp)\cdot\left(\frac{xp}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{P}$
$\Rightarrow k_P^{2} = x^{2}\cdot\dfrac{xP}{2}$
$x = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{2k_P^{2}}{P}}$

questions.stem: For a $\mathrm{Mg\,|\,Mg^{2+}(aq)\,||\,Ag^{+}(aq)\,|\,Ag}$ the correct Nernst Equation is :
questions.solution:
According to Nernst equation :-
$E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{RT}{nF}\ln Q$.
Cell reaction :-
$\mathrm{Mg_{(s)} + 2Ag^{+}_{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons 2Ag_{(s)} + Mg^{+2}_{(aq)}}$
$\Rightarrow Q = \dfrac{[\mathrm{Mg^{+2}}]}{[\mathrm{Ag^{+}}]^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow E = E^{\circ}_{Cell} - \dfrac{RT}{2F}\ln\left[\dfrac{[\mathrm{Mg^{+2}}]}{[\mathrm{Ag^{+}}]^{2}}\right]$

questions.stem:
$1.24$ g of $\mathrm{AX_2}$ (molar mass $124\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) is dissolved in 1 kg of water to form a solution with boiling point of $100.0156^\circ$C, while $25.4$ g of $\mathrm{AY_2}$ (molar mass $250\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) in 2 kg of water constitutes a solution with a boiling point of $100.0260^\circ$C.
$K_b(\mathrm{H_2O}) = 0.52\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$
Which of the following is correct ?
questions.solution:
For $\mathrm{AX_2}$ :- $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m \times i$
$0.0156 = 0.52 \times \dfrac{0.01}{1} \times i_{\mathrm{AX_2}}$
$\Rightarrow i_{\mathrm{AX_2}} = 3 \Rightarrow$ complete ionisation
For $\mathrm{AY_2}$ :- $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m \times i$
$0.026 = 0.52 \times 0.0508 \times i_{\mathrm{AY_2}}$
$\Rightarrow i_{\mathrm{AY_2}} \approx 1 \therefore$ complete unionisation

options.text: $\mathrm{AX_2}$ is completely unionised while $\mathrm{AY_2}$ is fully ionised.
$\mathrm{AX_2}$ is fully ionised while $\mathrm{AY_2}$ is completely unionised.

The reaction $\mathrm{A_2 + B_2 \rightarrow 2AB}$ follows the mechanism
$\mathrm{A_2 \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} A + A}$ (fast)
$\mathrm{A + B_2 \xrightarrow{k_2} AB + B}$ (slow)
$\mathrm{A + B \rightarrow AB}$ (fast)
The overall order of the reaction is :
questions.solution:
rate $= k_2[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B_2}]$ .......(1)
$\left(\dfrac{k_1}{k_{-1}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}]^{2}}{[\mathrm{A_2}]}\right)$
$\Rightarrow [\mathrm{A}] = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_1}{k_{-1}}}\cdot\sqrt{[\mathrm{A_2}]}$
Substituting in (1) ; we get
Rate $= k_2\sqrt{\dfrac{k_1}{k_{-1}}}\cdot[\mathrm{A_2}]^{\frac{1}{2}}\cdot[\mathrm{B_2}]$
$\therefore$ order $= \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 1.5$

questions.stem: If $a_0$ is denoted as the Bohr radius of hydrogen atom, then what is the de-Broglie wavelength ($\lambda$) of the electron present in the second orbit of hydrogen atom ? [n : any integer]
questions.solution:
$2\pi r_n = n\lambda$
$2\pi(4a_0) = n\lambda$
$= \lambda = \dfrac{8\pi a_0}{n}$

questions.stem:
Given below are some nitrogen containing compounds.
[four structures shown in figure: 4-nitroaniline, benzylamine ($\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$), acetanilide ($\mathrm{C_6H_5NHCOCH_3}$), aniline]
Each of them is treated with HCl separately. $1.0$ g of the most basic compound will consume ______mg of HCl.
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ C:12, H : 1, O : 16, Cl : 35.5)
questions.solution:
Benzyl Amine is most basic due to localised lone pair.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2 + HCl \longrightarrow C_6H_5CH_2NH_3^{\oplus}Cl^{\ominus}}$
Mole of benzyl amine $\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{107} = 0.00934$ mole
1 Mole of benzyl amine consumed 1 mole of HCl
So, Mole of HCl consumed $\rightarrow 0.00934$ mole
Mass of HCl consumed $\rightarrow 0.00934 \times$ molar mass of HCl
$= 0.00934 \times 36.5$
$= 0.341$ gm
$= 341$ mg
